findings.title: The duel continuation proof's 'missile in flight at the split' precondition becomes always true after Task 3
findings.claim: `tests/duelCheckpoint.test.ts` asserts `at.tactical.missiles.some((m) => m !== null)` as the precondition that the checkpoint continuation proof crosses an in-flight missile. After Task 3, `missiles` is a pool of `Missile` objects that are never null: a free entry is `emptyMissile()`. The assertion therefore passes whatever the state. The Task 2 codemod's missile regexes only rewrite `.missiles[<digit>]`, so they do not touch this line. Task 3 does not list or edit this file.
findings.evidence: tests/duelCheckpoint.test.ts:L39. Plan L2425 (`missiles: Slots<Missile>`). Plan L2480 (every entry is `emptyMissile()`). Plan L2461 (`emptyMissile` is an object with `active: false`). Plan L1534-1536 (the codemod regexes need a digit index). Task 3's files list, plan L1682, and its commit, plan L3591, omit tests/duelCheckpoint.test.ts. Contrast the replaced duelModules test at plan L1888, which correctly uses `m.active`.
findings.why: A test that passes for the wrong reason, on the riskiest R-2 path: checkpointing and restoring an in-flight pool entry with its owner. Today the split still has a missile because the rules are unchanged. The guard is still lost: a later change to SPLIT, the seed or the pool would silently drop the in-flight case from the continuation proof.
findings.fix: In Task 3 Step 1, add an exact replacement in tests/duelCheckpoint.test.ts: `expect(at.tactical.missiles.some((m) => m !== null), 'a missile in flight at the split').toBe(true);` becomes `expect(at.tactical.missiles.some((m) => m.active), 'a missile in flight at the split').toBe(true);`. Add the file to Task 3's Modify list and to its `git add` line.

findings.title: No targeted test pins owner-order missile resolution when pool entries are out of owner order
findings.claim: Task 3 resolves missiles in owner order through `missileOf`, which is correct. But the only proof that order is preserved is the oracle's per-tick events digest. That catches a reordering only when two missiles end on the same tick, through expiry, a missile-missile meeting, or both landing. The plan never shows that the 20 runs contain such a tick with the entries swapped. The new pool tests check entry assignment, not resolution order.
findings.evidence: Plan L2963-2985 (resolveMissiles by owner, events pushed in that order). Plan L1785-1802 (the pool test covers placement and freeing only). Plan L54 (Decision 5 cites 7,331 ticks with the enemy's missile in entry 0, not simultaneous endings). Plan L452 (order is observable only through `JSON.stringify([results, d.tactical.events, d.events])`). Old order: missiles.ts:L63-80.
findings.why: Per the review brief, a reordering that the 20 runs happen not to exercise must still be caught. A later refactor that iterates `state.missiles` in entry order instead of using `missileOf` per slot would pass the oracle unless such a tick exists.
findings.fix: Add a case to tests/tacticalSlots.test.ts. Call `launchMissile(st, 1)` then `launchMissile(st, 0)`, so the enemy is in entry 0 and the crew in entry 1. Place both well clear of every body with `age = MISSILE_LIFE_TICKS - 1`, call `resolveMissiles(st)`, and expect the `missileEnd` events' `ship` values to be `[0, 1]`. Add a second case that places the two missiles touching: expect causes `['missile', 'missile']` in the order ship 0, ship 1, and both entries freed.

findings.title: The duel snapshot validator does not pin the duel's slot identity (active, cls, target)
findings.claim: `validateTacticalValues` accepts any slot layout that is internally consistent. Slot 1 can be marked inactive and zeroed. `systems.i.cls` can swap classes within 0..1, and `systems.i.target` can point at the slot itself. `validateDuelSnapshot` adds no duel-specific check, so a forged or corrupted checkpoint restores into a state the duel never creates. With slot 1 inactive, `others` is empty, so `enemyDown` is false and the duel cannot end by the hunter's death. With slot 1 given the Cutter class, `hunterSlot` returns -1 and the enemy is never flown.
findings.evidence: Plan L2714-2738 (the validator: inactive slots need only zeros) and L2692-2697 (`cls: within(0, SHIP_CLASSES.length - 1)`, `target: within(0, slots - 1)`). Plan L3134-3135 (`others` is filtered by active; `enemyDown = others.length > 0 && …`). Plan L3112 (hunterSlot by AI profile). Plan L3484 (snapshot.ts only checks the returned length). snapshot.ts:L60-72.
findings.why: R-1b's validator refuses values the duel cannot produce, such as an empty missile slot holding values or out-of-range headingAcc. R-2 adds identity fields that are constants for the duel but leaves them loosely bounded, so the 'slot invariants' brief item is only partly carried over.
findings.fix: In Task 3 Step 4, add a check to `validateDuelSnapshot` after `validateTacticalValues`, with offsets taken from `TACTICAL_MODULES` field names. Require `ships.length === 2`, `ships.0.active === ships.1.active === 1`, `systems.i.cls === DUEL_CLASSES[i]` and `systems.i.target === 1 - i`. Add the matching cases to the duelSnapshot test list, for example `['systems.1.cls', 0, 0, /duel slot/]`.

findings.title: Spec §5's 'present: [b, b]' and two-ship telemetry stay pairs without a stated deviation
findings.claim: Spec §5 lists `present: [b, b]` and the two-ship render models among the pair assumptions that become arrays. The plan leaves duel presence a fixed pair. Telemetry also stays two-ship: `[crew, enemy] = tac.ships`, `for (let i = 0; i < 2; i++)`, `laserOn = [false, false]`, and `DuelTelemetry.ships` and `terminal` as pairs. No Decision says so or gives the reason.
findings.evidence: Spec L105-108. Plan Decisions L46-63 never mention presence or telemetry pairs. sim/duel/telemetry.ts:L93, L96, L107, L111, L153 are untouched apart from the replacements at plan L883-949. sim/duel/modules.ts:L19 (presence is per player).
findings.why: The plan must state where it deviates from the spec. Presence is per player, not per ship, so keeping it a pair is probably right, but a later reader cannot tell a deliberate scope cut from an omission.
findings.fix: Add a Decision, for example number 15: duel presence is per player (two players), not per ship, so it stays `[b, b]`. `DuelTelemetry` and its `i < 2` loops stay a crew-and-enemy record of the duel until R-5 gives encounters N ships. List the remaining sites.

findings.title: Body-only comparisons in tacticalSoloFlight silently stop covering the systems record
findings.claim: `plain(st.ships[i])` compared every field of a ship before R-2. After Task 3 it compares only the body. 'ship 1 never moves', 'flies straight through ship 1' and 'matches stepFlight for ship 0' no longer cover hull, rooms or shields. The Task 3 edits to this file change only the `hitStatics` call.
findings.evidence: tests/tacticalSoloFlight.test.ts:L7, L16, L28, L37; plan L2195-2209.
findings.why: A small loss of coverage. For example, stepSoloFlight could charge ship 0's hull differently from stepFlight and L37 would no longer notice.
findings.fix: In Task 3, extend these assertions to compare the systems record too: `expect(st.systems[1]).toEqual(beforeSystems)` and `expect(a.systems[0]).toEqual(b.systems[0])`.

findings.title: The oracle never checks the values of the declared-added fields
findings.claim: `ships.length`, `ships.<i>.active`, `systems.<i>.cls` and `systems.<i>.target` are declared added. `aliasPlan` only checks that they exist, and `recordRun` keeps only the baseline's names, so their values are never compared at any tick. Most mistakes would show up in other fields, but not all: a run whose target or cls flips with no effect within the cap would go unnoticed.
findings.evidence: Plan L3567 (`added`). Plan L404-407 (new fields only need to be declared). Plan L435 (only the target schema's names are kept).
findings.why: The proof holds the moved fields to the old values, but nothing pins the new constants to the duel's values.
findings.fix: In tests/tacticalSlots.test.ts, or in recordRun when `schema.migration` is set, assert every tick that `ships.length === 2`, `active` is `[1, 1]`, `cls` is `[0, 1]` and `target` is `[1, 0]` across a full scripted run.

findings.title: The codemod's import sort depends on the locale
findings.claim: The codemod sorts merged import names with `localeCompare` and no locale, so the result depends on Node's default ICU locale. Later exact replacements depend on that order, for example `import { missileOf, Outcome }` at plan L1976.
findings.evidence: Plan L1542 (`a.replace(/^type /, '').localeCompare(b.replace(/^type /, ''))`). Plan L1976 (Task 3's old text relies on that order).
findings.why: A fresh executor whose locale orders mixed case differently would get an import line that Task 3's exact old text does not match.
findings.fix: Use `localeCompare(…, 'en')` in the codemod. Otherwise state that the expected output assumes the en locale.
